localization_scope: English and Simplified Chinese include the current BigMac2 addition. French, Russian, German and Japanese retain the prior 175-paper snapshot. PDF content is unchanged.

hero_illustration.depiction: Symbolic intellectual confrontation between AI and the Fields Medal tradition; not a real award, endorsement, or contest result.

scope: Original 175-paper archive plus 55 nonduplicated gated BigMac2 manuscripts; five further gated BigMac2 drafts map to existing canonical papers. Partial results do not settle their parent problems.
upload_notice: Git distribution excludes manuscript LaTeX via .gitignore; PDFs and selected reproduction code/evidence remain. Local files are not deleted.

papers.title: The Tang–Zhang Schatten Norm Formula Fails Below the Hilbertian Exponent
papers.problem_definition: Determine the optimal constant $c_p(m)$ in $\lVert\sum_k A_k\rVert_p\le c_p(m)\lVert\sum_k\lvert A_k\rvert\rVert_p$ for complex matrices, and test Tang–Zhang's explicit equiangular candidate formula. The second stage asks whether a counterexample at one exponent extends to an interval.
papers.contribution: **Counterexamples and sharp positive results.** Constructs real $2\times2$ rank-one counterexamples for every $1<p<2$, with a fixed certificate consisting of seven strict rational inequalities at $p=3/2$. Identifies a transverse local transition at $p=2$. Establishes sharp bounds and equality cases for rank-at-most-one summands when $p\ge2$, and handles arbitrary complex matrices when $m=2,p=4$. The remaining arbitrary-rank cases are not resolved.

papers.title: The Exact Schatten 3/2 Constant for Two Rank-One Matrices
papers.problem_definition: Find the exact best constant in $\lVert A+B\rVert_{3/2}\le C\lVert\lvert A\rvert+\lvert B\rvert\rVert_{3/2}$ for real $2\times2$ rank-one matrices, and classify equality.
papers.contribution: **Exact solution of the specified subproblem.** Obtains $C_*=[(107+51\sqrt{17})/256]^{1/6}$, in fact for complex rank-at-most-one matrices in every dimension $n\ge2$, with attainment already in real dimension two. Includes equality classification, algebraic isolation, a minimal polynomial, and a strict comparison with the Tang–Zhang candidate.

papers.title: Sharp Self-Chollet Inequalities in Order Five: Rank Two and Structured Rank Three
papers.problem_definition: For real correlation matrices $C$ of order five, study $R(C)=\operatorname{per}(C\circ C)/\operatorname{per}(C)^2$. Determine the rank-two optimum and investigate whether rank at most three admits a uniform bound strictly below one.
papers.contribution: **Complete rank-two result; structured rank-three results.** The sharp rank-two constant is $137/1440$, attained by a projective regular pentagon. Two infinite rank-three families have sharp value $13/48$, with the corresponding configuration a strict local maximum in the full rank-three configuration space. Also treats coherence at most $27/50$ and, without a rank restriction, minimum eigenvalue at least $3/4$. Neither the global rank-three optimum nor the general order-five conjecture is settled.

papers.title: Closing the Permanent-Rank Boundary for the Alon–Jaeger–Tarsi Conjecture
papers.problem_definition: For every $M\in\mathrm{GL}_8(\mathbb F_5)$, must there be a vector $x$ such that every coordinate of both $x$ and $Mx$ is nonzero?
papers.contribution: **Full-proof claim in the manuscript; key dependencies require independent rechecking.** Splits by permanent rank and combines Yu's recurrence and the Combinatorial Nullstellensatz with a Kisley–Shader equality classification. Claims the range $n\le2^{p-2}$ for primes $p\ge5$, including the stated problem. The field assumptions, quantifiers, monomial-equivalence hypotheses, and transition between these ingredients remain priorities for independent verification; archival inclusion is not certification of this claim.

papers.title: A Witness-Core Reduction for the Rank-Four, Covering-Number-Three Case of Chvátal’s Conjecture
papers.problem_definition: For a downset $\mathcal D$ of rank at most four and an intersecting subfamily $\mathcal F$ with covering number three, prove $\#\mathcal F\le\max_i\#\{A\in\mathcal D:i\in A\}$.
papers.contribution: **Structural reduction, not a solution of the original inequality.** A three-cover and witnesses to its minimality yield a core of at most ten points; every member contains at least two core points, leaving external rank at most two. Classifies 29 core isomorphism types and reduces the problem to 29 colored rank-two external problems. Supplies section formulas, rigidity lemmas, and a finite Boolean encoding.

papers.title: Diagonal Loading and Low-Rank Strata at the First Open Order of Lieb’s Permanental-Dominance Conjecture
papers.problem_definition: Compare $\operatorname{Imm}_\lambda(A)/\chi_\lambda(e)$ with $\operatorname{per}(A)$ for $14\times14$ Hermitian positive semidefinite matrices, particularly on low-rank Gram strata.
papers.contribution: **Low-rank obstructions and structured positive results.** Following the shape-theorem reduction used in the manuscript, the remaining partition is $\lambda=(4,4,3,3)$, whose immanant vanishes at rank at most three. Handles Gram matrices on four projective directions, closure under nonnegative diagonal loading, and local stability near the diagonal equality stratum. Diagonal loading also gives positive-definite examples. The unrestricted remaining case is not solved.

papers.title: Exact Local Rigidity of a Rank-23 Decomposition of the 3×3 Matrix-Multiplication Tensor over F₂
papers.problem_definition: Determine the exact tensor rank of $3\times3$ matrix multiplication over $\mathbb F_2$: seek a decomposition of rank at most 22 or a stronger global lower bound.
papers.contribution: **Local irreducibility of one fixed decomposition.** For the frozen rank-23 decomposition, the sum of any selection of at most eight summands has tensor rank equal to the number selected, so it cannot be replaced by fewer multiplications. Checks 880,946 subsets and all 729 Brent identities exactly. This does not establish that the full tensor has rank 23.

papers.title: A Quantifier Obstruction in an SDP Test for the PPT-Squared Conjecture
papers.problem_definition: Must the composition of two PPT quantum channels on a four-dimensional system be entanglement-breaking? Assess an SDP formulation proposed for counterexample searches.
papers.contribution: **A correction to the optimization formulation.** Proves that the audited minimization of distance to the decomposable cone is identically zero; imposing trace preservation does not fix the problem. Derives a maximization test with the correct quantifiers, an exact dual distance formula, and a bilinear formulation. Structured tests and 440 corrected searches produced no exact counterexample. The four-dimensional conjecture remains unresolved by this paper.

papers.title: Tuza’s Conjecture for Split Graphs with an Eight-Vertex Clique Part and Two Neighborhood Types
papers.problem_definition: Prove $\tau_\triangle(G)\le2\nu_\triangle(G)$ for split or interval graphs, where the parameters denote minimum triangle edge-cover size and maximum edge-disjoint triangle packing size.
papers.contribution: **An infinite subclass of split graphs.** Proves the inequality when a specified clique part has eight vertices and the independent side has at most two triangle-active neighborhood types, with arbitrary multiplicities. Multiplicity truncation and symmetry reduction yield 44,702 canonical cases with explicit covers, packings, and independent verification. Also gives a maximum-cut sufficient condition for sparse 2-shadows. General split and interval graphs are not settled.

papers.title: Exact Gram Obstructions and Five-Row Local Optimality in the Order-23 Maximal Determinant Problem
papers.problem_definition: Determine $D(23)=\max_{H\in\{\pm1\}^{23\times23}}\lvert\det H\rvert$, by improving the best construction or excluding every larger determinant.
papers.contribution: **Gram obstructions and local optimality.** For the manuscript's record value $L=2{,}779{,}447{,}296{,}000{,}000$, rules out sign-Gram realizations of all order-23 Ehlich block candidates with determinant exceeding $L^2$. Classifies 1,255 block partitions and treats a class within six edge toggles of a balanced Ehlich graph. Certifies that simultaneously replacing at most five rows or five columns of the frozen record matrix cannot improve its determinant, covering 33,649 five-subsets. The global value of $D(23)$ is not determined.

papers.title: Rank-Two Cases of the Order-Four Soules Permanent-on-Top Problem
papers.problem_definition: For $4\times4$ Hermitian positive semidefinite matrices, test $\lambda_{\max}(\Pi(A))\le\operatorname{per}(A)$ for the Schur power matrix $\Pi(A)$, starting with rank at most two.
papers.contribution: **Complete real rank-two result; partial complex rank-two results.** Establishes the real case. In the complex case, controls the $(2,2)$ representation block and gives a sharp trace bound for the $(3,1)$ block, reducing the remaining question to an explicit $3\times3$ determinant inequality. Also handles coplanar Bloch configurations and one noncoplanar cyclic family. The full complex rank-two and unrestricted order-four cases are not settled.

papers.title: Certified Nonextension of a Hadamard Pair to a MUB Triple in Dimension Six
papers.problem_definition: For an explicit member $K$ of a complex Hadamard family of order six, determine whether the standard basis and $K/\sqrt6$ can be extended by a third mutually unbiased basis.
papers.contribution: **Nonextension for the selected pair.** For a fixed Matolcsi–Szőllősi family member, exhaustive interval isolation yields 52 common unbiased rays. A conservative orthogonality graph has 48 edges and no triangle, hence no six-clique capable of forming a third basis. Gives an exact extendible construction at the endpoint $x=-1$. This does not decide whether any four mutually unbiased bases exist in dimension six.

papers.title: Multiplicity-Isolated Cores and Chromatic Symmetric Reconstruction of Trees
papers.problem_definition: For trees of diameter six, determine whether equality of chromatic symmetric functions, $X_T=X_{T'}$, forces $T\cong T'$.
papers.contribution: **Reconstruction of an infinite subclass.** Reconstructs proper trees when every nonleaf vertex of the weighted leaf-component core has a weight appearing nowhere else; core-leaf weights may repeat arbitrarily. Uses only the leading star-basis partition and adjacent coefficients. Covers an infinite diameter-six subclass and gives a canonical parameterization for general diameter-six trees. The full diameter-six problem is not solved.

papers.title: Proof-Carrying Reductions for 4-Regular Girth-Nine Graphs of Excess Four
papers.problem_definition: Determine the cage number $n(4,9)$, beginning with whether a 4-regular graph on 165 vertices can have girth at least nine.
papers.contribution: **Necessary conditions and verifiable finite reductions.** Derives a distance-five commutation identity and a lower bound of 2,825 nine-cycles. In the equality case, excludes a support branch of length 13 and reduces the length-11 branch to four local witnesses. Provides 134 external-data orbits, 21 matching types, and 61,236 independently reconstructed forbidden eight-cycle witnesses. These reductions do not decide existence on 165 vertices.

papers.title: A Nine-Unit Fiber Floor in a Full Three-Cover Branch of Frankl’s Conjecture
papers.problem_definition: In the empty-set-free, height-five minimal-counterexample setting for Frankl's union-closed sets conjecture, analyze the full minimal three-cover branch. Here $q_0$ is the empty-private-support fiber size and $q_2$ is the total excess of the three double-private-coordinate fibers.
papers.contribution: **A conditional infinite-class theorem.** Proves $q_0+q_2\ge9$ and reduces the first residual point $(r,t)=(10,27)$ to the unique parameter triple $(q_0,u,q_2)=(4,0,6)$. Uses deletion-block injections, cross-fiber intersections, capacity saturation, and a near-extremal classification at height three with five generators. The archived 45-page final manuscript supersedes the earlier block-projection version. It does not settle the full height-five case or Frankl's conjecture.

papers.title: Coset and Fiber Constructions for Rainbow Trees in Finite Abelian Groups
papers.problem_definition: Study a group-valued form of the Graham–Sloane harmonious-tree problem: construct vertex labels whose sums on edge endpoints are pairwise distinct, and develop composable infinite classes.
papers.contribution: **Conditional construction theorems.** Gives permutation leaf extensions over subgroup cosets, an attachment classification within that model, and circulant-permanent counts. For odd-order quotient groups, combines independent fiber trees in arbitrary Abelian extensions, allows distinct missing colors, and iterates the construction to obtain infinite families. Does not solve the unrestricted harmonious-tree conjecture or its stronger bijective cyclic form.

papers.title: Odd-Order Trees with Exactly Three Vertices of Degree Two Are Edge-Graceful
papers.problem_definition: Does every odd-order tree with exactly three degree-two vertices admit a bijection from its edges to $1,\ldots,n-1$ such that the sums of incident edge labels at vertices are pairwise distinct modulo $n$?
papers.contribution: **Complete solution of the specified subclass.** Roots the tree at a degree-two vertex, turning the other two into nonadjacent single-child blocks, and supplies a same-parent two-child-block gadget. A symbolic argument covers all odd $n\ge25$. The remaining 1,061,384 unlabeled trees of order at most 23 are covered by explicit exact certificates, independent labeling verification, and census-set equality checks. This is not a solution of Lee's conjecture for all odd-order trees.

papers.title: No Centrally Symmetric Hexagon Attains the Planar L2 Rogers–Shephard Bound
papers.problem_definition: For planar convex bodies containing the origin, investigate the sharp Rogers–Shephard inequality for the Firey $L_p$ sum with the reflected body.
papers.contribution: **Strict inequality for a full geometric family.** Proves that every centrally symmetric hexagon, with any admissible origin placement, lies strictly below the planar $p=2$ bound $(2+\pi/2)\operatorname{area}(K)$. Affine normalization and exact area-deficit formulas exclude equality throughout this family. The all-body, all-$p$ problem remains unresolved.

papers.title: A CRT Carrier Bound for an LCM Recurrence: Exact Verification Through 1,000,000,000,002
papers.problem_definition: Let $x(1)=1$, $x(n)=2x(n-1)+\operatorname{lcm}(x(n-1),n)$, and $a(n)=x(n+1)/x(n)-2$. Must $a(p-1)=p$ whenever $p$ is prime and $p-2$ is not prime?
papers.contribution: **Certified finite range and a structural reduction.** Proves the assertion for every eligible prime $p\le10^{12}+2$. Chinese-remainder carrier certificates for primes through $10^6$ avoid direct generation of the enormous recurrence terms. The assertion for all primes remains open in this work.

papers.title: An Exact Ten-Billion-Term Boundary for Jumps 14 and 15 and the First Jump 16 in OEIS A260194
papers.problem_definition: For $a_1=a_2=a_3=1$ and $a_{n+1}=a_n+\gcd(a_n,a_{n-2})$, investigate which positive integers occur as jumps $a_{n+1}-a_n$.
papers.contribution: **Exact computational boundary.** Locates the first jump of size 16 at $n=399{,}815{,}271$, and excludes jumps 14 and 15 through $n=9{,}999{,}999{,}999$. Independently structured exact implementations check the result. Finite nonoccurrence is not a proof that these jumps never occur.

papers.title: A Proof That Every Integer Occurs Infinitely Often as a Difference of Binary and Ternary Digit Sums
papers.problem_definition: Writing $s_b(n)$ for the base-$b$ digit sum, does every integer $z$ occur infinitely often as $s_3(n)-s_2(n)$?
papers.contribution: **Historical full-proof manuscript.** Extends the residue-selection step in the binary–ternary collision argument to arbitrary fixed offsets, yielding infinitely many solutions for each $z\in\mathbb Z$. The argument is qualitative and gives no effective bound for the least solution. This legacy manuscript is retained without claiming a fresh current-workflow audit.

papers.title: A Proof of Two Endpoint Doubling Breaks in the Divisor Lists of Odd Composite Integers
papers.problem_definition: For the ordered positive divisors $1=d_1<\cdots<d_t=m$, let $A(m)$ be one plus the number of adjacent pairs with odd $d_{i+1}\ge2d_i$. Is $A(m)\ge3$ for every Carmichael number?
papers.contribution: **Historical elementary proof, with a stronger domain.** Establishes $A(m)\ge3$ for every odd composite integer: the first and last divisor adjacencies supply two distinct doubling breaks. This settles the stated inequality, not a classification of all divisor gaps; it should not be counted as a new deep conjecture merely because a PDF exists.

papers.title: A Counterexample to the 2-4-6-8 Binomial Representation Conjecture
papers.problem_definition: Can every positive integer be written as $\binom{W}{2}+\binom{X}{4}+\binom{Y}{6}+\binom{Z}{8}$ with all four upper indices at least two?
papers.contribution: **Historical exact counterexample verification.** Certifies nonrepresentability of $896315812331399$ using 2,755,643,831 exact perfect-square tests and an independent recomputation. The manuscript credits an earlier public identification of this candidate. It does not claim discovery priority or minimality of the counterexample.

papers.title: Primorial-Cube Bounds and an Explicit Obstruction for a Powerful-Core Majorant of k sigma(k) Fibers
papers.problem_definition: Bound the number of integers $k$ satisfying $k\sigma(k)=N$, using the necessary powerful-core condition $P\sigma(P)\mid N$.
papers.contribution: **A proved limitation of one proposed approach.** The powerful-core majorant is small on primorial cubes, but an explicit infinite family makes it at least $\exp((\log 2/4+o(1))\log N/\log\log N)$. Thus this majorant alone cannot give the proposed smaller-scale bound. No corresponding lower bound for the actual solution fibers is claimed.

papers.title: A Computer-Assisted Proof that k(18)=34
papers.problem_definition: What is the smallest number $k(18)$ of distinct integer denominators, all at least 18, whose reciprocals sum to one?
papers.contribution: **Historical exact finite optimum: $k(18)=34$.** Supplies a 34-term identity and excludes every shorter representation using harmonic bounds, exact rational search, and prime-power coverage pruning. The manuscript states its replay boundary explicitly. The associated asymptotic problem and historical priority are not settled.

papers.title: KG(8,2) as a counterexample to coverage by two graphs of fractional chromatic number at most 5/2
papers.problem_definition: Can the edges of the Kneser graph $KG(8,2)$ be covered by two spanning subgraphs, each having fractional chromatic number at most $5/2$?
papers.contribution: **Historical negative resolution with a quantitative gap.** Every such cover has a layer with fractional chromatic number at least $28/11>5/2$. The finite proof classifies independent-set witnesses and excludes 728 symmetry-reduced Boolean cases. The lower bound is not claimed to be sharp.

papers.title: An explicit proof of the existence of a proper Euler magic matrix of order seven
papers.problem_definition: Does a proper Euler magic matrix of order seven exist: an integer matrix with orthogonal equal-norm rows, matching diagonal square sums, and 49 distinct entry squares?
papers.contribution: **Historical explicit construction.** Gives a complete integer matrix with common squared norm $4{,}793{,}786{,}401{,}980{,}625$. A Householder-and-rotation construction explains the witness; direct integer arithmetic verifies every requirement. No minimality or general-order theorem is claimed.

papers.title: A Sharp Fixed-Defect Conjecture for Fractional Gaussian Traces
papers.problem_definition: For fractional Gaussian binomial series, is the integer trace at parameter $1/2$ coefficientwise at least the trace at $1/4$, for every positive integer index?
papers.contribution: **Historical conjecture paper, not a solution.** Proposes a sharp ten-term fixed-defect correction, necessary already at index 13, and proves that its uniform validity would imply the trace comparison. Archived exact tests reach index 1004; independent reconstruction has explicitly smaller coverage. Stabilization proves the bounded-degree extension, not the full conjecture.

papers.title: A Computer-Assisted Proof of the Oriented Ramsey Value k(3,4)=21
papers.problem_definition: What is the least order $k(3,4)$ forcing every oriented graph to contain an independent triple or a complete transitive four-vertex tournament?
papers.contribution: **Historical certificate-backed proof of $k(3,4)=21$.** Combines a known order-20 construction with 129 upper-bound templates, checked classification refutations, and reversal transports. The audit corrected a defect in the original LRAT checker before replaying the selected corpus. The manuscript acknowledges an earlier assertion of the same value and makes no priority claim.

papers.title: A Mobius–Descartes Proof of Unique Root Location for an Eighth-Degree Stationary Polynomial
papers.problem_definition: For every $0<q<1$ and $s,t>0$, does the specified degree-eight stationary polynomial for a weighted-shift numerical-radius problem have exactly one real root in $(1/3,1)$?
papers.contribution: **Complete parameter-uniform proof, strengthened to simplicity.** The substitution $z=(x+1)/(x+3)$ turns the root-location question into a one-sign-variation problem. Exact coefficient identities and positive Bernstein certificates permit Descartes' rule to prove that the target root exists uniquely and has multiplicity one.

papers.title: A Large-Tandem Model for an Unresolved Canon-Avoidance Sequence
papers.problem_definition: Determine the enumeration of the specified canon-avoiding word family, whose positional constraints define a finite poset for each size.
papers.contribution: **Structural classification rather than a closed enumeration.** Identifies the family with large-tandem quarter-plane excursions, proves that its generating function is not D-finite, and obtains the corresponding asymptotic order. Exact independent encodings agree through index 11. The requested exact univariate enumeration is not supplied.

papers.title: Seven-Strand T0 Crossing Matrices of Positive Pure Braids: An Exact Exhaustive Resolution
papers.problem_definition: Is every symmetric, nonnegative integer $7\times7$ zero-diagonal matrix satisfying the stated $T_0$ zero condition the directed crossing matrix of a positive pure braid?
papers.contribution: **Complete seven-strand resolution.** Exhaustively checks the Boolean support layer across all $2^{21}$ masks, with explicit positive braid words and independent crossing-matrix verifiers. Published lifting results and a reproduced transfer argument extend the certificates to arbitrary nonnegative integer entries. The theorem is specifically for seven strands.

papers.title: Certified Non-Sharpness of a Hankel Bound for π/3-Spirallike Convex Functions
papers.problem_definition: Determine the sharp Hankel-determinant bound $M_{\pi/3}$ for the specified class of $\pi/3$-spirallike convex functions.
papers.contribution: **Certified improvement, not the exact optimum.** Establishes $9291/320000<M_{\pi/3}<4181/144000$, proving the earlier estimate $89/2880$ non-sharp. An exact Schur-parameter reduction, a rational witness, and rational branch-and-bound leave a gap below $3.5\times10^{-7}$.

papers.title: Integral Homology of the Multiplicity-11 Singleton Stratum
papers.problem_definition: Compute the integral homology of the frozen multiplicity-11 singleton-stratum complex $C_*(11;d)$ for every odd $d\ge11$.
papers.contribution: **Complete all-degree classification.** The homology is $\mathbb Z$ only at $(d,j)=(11,1)$ and vanishes otherwise. A geometric factorization identifies the stratum; an explicit contraction of its one-point compactification handles every higher degree. Exact boundary and Smith computations corroborate the first cases.

papers.title: Arbitrarily Delayed Continuation Splits in an Exact Lehmer-Signature Graph
papers.problem_definition: Can the exact Lehmer-signature extension graph for the specified avoidance class be reduced using a fixed finite horizon of continuation data?
papers.contribution: **An infinite-family obstruction to bounded-horizon minimization.** Constructs reachable signature pairs agreeing on every continuation shorter than $m$ but splitting precisely at length $m$, for arbitrary $m\ge4$. This rules out that fixed-horizon approach, not every polynomial-time counting algorithm; the original enumeration problem remains unresolved.

papers.title: The Exponent Two Is Not Optimal for a Two-Dimensional Critical Hardy Stability Inequality
papers.problem_definition: Is exponent two optimal in the stated two-dimensional critical Hardy stability inequality involving an exponential-Orlicz norm and normalized defect?
papers.contribution: **Universal disproof of the proposed optimal exponent.** Proves admissibility of every $q>1$ using an explicit $L^2$ remainder and subcritical exponential interpolation. Consequently the infimum exponent satisfies $q_*\le1$, so it cannot equal two. The paper does not determine whether $q_*=1$.

papers.title: Projective Signed-Permutation Classification of Exact Score Ties in the 2,285-State Plastic Closure
papers.problem_definition: Within the fixed 2,285-state plastic-closure archive, characterize when distinct admissible candidates have exactly equal scores and recover the minimum-score ties.
papers.contribution: **Exact classification on the archived domain.** Score equality is equivalent to a projective signed-permutation relation; exact invariants classify 2,974,862 candidates and recover all 156 minimum-tie states. The conclusion remains conditional on the archived verification-key map for 482 rows whose underlying raw logs were unavailable.

papers.title: No Cubic Annihilators for Canonical Coordinates of Permutations of F2 in Dimension 4
papers.problem_definition: Are the canonical multilinear coordinate polynomials of every permutation of $\mathbb F_2^4$ algebraically independent as formal polynomials?
papers.contribution: **A strict lower bound on any possible relation.** Rules out every nonzero annihilating polynomial of total degree at most three. Affine-group orbit reduction and independently checked UNSAT certificates cover the cubic cases. Relations of degree four or higher are not excluded, so the full algebraic-independence problem remains unresolved.

papers.title: The Gabor System G(Q2, 8/21, 7/4) Is a Frame
papers.problem_definition: For the triangular B-spline $Q_2(x)=\max(1-\lvert x\rvert,0)$, is the Gabor system with translation step $8/21$ and modulation step $7/4$ a frame for $L^2(\mathbb R)$?
papers.contribution: **Exact positive resolution at the specified parameters.** Proves full rank of the associated $2\times3$ Zibulski–Zeevi matrix everywhere on its fundamental torus. Rational support cells, Laurent-polynomial minors, and exact gcd checks handle both interiors and boundaries; compactness gives a positive frame lower bound.

papers.title: A Faithful-C₉ Tensor Exclusion through Base Order 188 for Navarro's Character-Field Question
papers.problem_definition: In Navarro's character-field question, can a faithful cyclic-order-nine tensor factor produce a counterexample of smaller order than the known benchmark?
papers.contribution: **Complete exclusion of one finite mechanism.** For every base group of order at most 188, excludes the faithful-$C_9$ external-product mechanism under the specified eligibility condition. Exact character-field computations cover 4,423 base groups and 1,073,220 faithful-factor choices. The global minimum counterexample order is not determined.

papers.title: A Computer-Assisted Type Bound through Multiplicity Thirteen for Five-Generated Nearly Gorenstein Numerical Semigroups
papers.problem_definition: How large can the type of a five-generated nearly Gorenstein numerical semigroup be, and where can type five first occur?
papers.contribution: **A sharp multiplicity cutoff for the stronger bound.** Proves type at most four for multiplicity at most 13 using unbounded Kunz-coordinate integer constraints. The semigroup $\langle14,19,29,39,44\rangle$ supplies an exact type-five example at multiplicity 14. This does not settle the unrestricted type bound.

papers.title: Compatible Three-Qubit Spin Alignment Along a Diagonal Segment
papers.problem_definition: For compatible two-body marginals of an arbitrary three-qubit state, does the specified equal-weight spin-alignment majorization hold for $Q_q=\operatorname{diag}(q,1-q)$ throughout $1/2\le q\le1$?
papers.contribution: **Complete proof along the prescribed segment.** Combines the established $q=1/2$ endpoint with the pure-state endpoint at $q=1$. Ky Fan convexity and exact affine behavior of the aligned target establish every required partial-sum inequality. The result retains compatibility and equal-weight assumptions.

papers.title: A Top-Power-Form Obstruction for the Four-Vertex Path and Star Edge-Span Algebras
papers.problem_definition: Are the four-vertex path and star edge-span algebras over $\mathbb Q$ isomorphic as unital graded algebras?
papers.contribution: **A distinct short obstruction, not a newly discovered nonisomorphism.** Their degree-nine top-power forms have incompatible factorization types: six linear factors versus three squared linear factors and an absolutely irreducible cubic. The manuscript explicitly acknowledges that nonisomorphism already follows from a broader public reconstruction argument.

papers.title: Unimodality of the Fourth-Order q-Fibonomial Coefficients
papers.problem_definition: Are the coefficients of the fourth-order $q$-Fibonomial polynomial $\{m+4\brack4\}_{F,q}$ unimodal for every integer $m\ge1$?
papers.contribution: **Complete proof of the fourth-order slice.** Reduces lower-half coefficient differences to four evaluations of an explicit partition denumerant. Residue bounds prove every $m\ge7$, and exact certificates cover the six remaining values. The unrestricted two-parameter $q$-Fibonomial conjecture is not settled.

papers.title: The Five-Weight Case of a Bernoulli Threshold Conjecture
papers.problem_definition: For five positive weights summing to one and independent Bernoulli$(p)$ variables, is $\Pr(\sum_i w_iX_i\ge p)\ge p$ throughout $0\le p\le1/3$?
papers.contribution: **Complete five-weight theorem.** Classifies the reduced threshold families through star-or-triangle structure of the nonqualifying-pair graph, then proves the probability inequalities by exact factorization. Includes equality-threshold boundary faces. Other dimensions and the range $p>1/3$ are outside the result.

papers.title: The Unique Level-11 Maximizer for Finite Gilbreath Extension Sets
papers.problem_definition: Among increasing level-11 Gilbreath sequences beginning $(2,3)$, which sequence admits the largest complete integer extension set?
papers.contribution: **Exact optimum and unique extremizer.** Exhaustively treats all 17,535,396 sequences and proves that the maximum extension-set size is 1025, attained only by $(2,3,5,9,17,33,65,129,257,513,1025)$. The extension variable ranges over all integers. No all-level extremal theorem is claimed.

papers.title: Rectangular Harmonic Congruences in Inert Imaginary Quadratic Orders
papers.problem_definition: For endpoint-inclusive unit rectangles in imaginary quadratic orders, prove the specified first- and second-reciprocal-sum congruences at every inert unramified prime $p>5$ and every depth $k\ge1$.
papers.contribution: **Complete congruence theorem in the stated domain.** Establishes divisibility by $p^{2k}$ for the first sum and by $p^k$ for the second. Negation pairing supplies the missing base-case factor, and an exact block decomposition gives simultaneous induction. Split or ramified primes and stronger exponents are not covered.

papers.title: An explicit degree-3059 Littlewood multiple of 1+x2+x3+x8+x9+x10
papers.problem_definition: Does $1+x^2+x^3+x^8+x^9+x^{10}$ divide a degree-3059 polynomial all of whose coefficients are $+1$ or $-1$?
papers.contribution: **Explicit positive certificate.** Supplies an integer quotient of degree 3049 and verifies all 3060 product coefficients, with independent monic long division. This answers the specified degree-3059 existence question, without claiming that 3059 is the minimum possible degree.

papers.title: Sixth-order log-determinant convexity for two-dimensional split covariance intersection
papers.problem_definition: For two-dimensional split covariance intersection, is the sixth derivative of $\log\det P(w)$ nonnegative for every $0<w<1$ and every admissible positive-semidefinite input quadruple?
papers.contribution: **Complete sixth-order inequality, including singular inputs.** Ordered eigenvalue crossings control the determinant roots and yield the derivative bound through reciprocal sixth powers. Continuity of rational Taylor coefficients extends the argument to the allowed singular boundary. Higher dimensions and other derivative orders are not asserted.

papers.title: Half letter frequency and balanced borders for one forbidden binary word
papers.problem_definition: For uniformly chosen binary words avoiding one nonempty forbidden word $w$, does the limiting mean frequency of ones equal $1/2$ exactly when every nonempty border of $w$ is balanced?
papers.contribution: **Complete equivalence.** A first-occurrence generating function and a finite-sum dominance argument exclude half-frequency whenever any border is unbalanced, even with arbitrarily many mixed-sign border imbalances. Balanced borders give exact finite-length balance. Separate ordering and related-frequency conjectures are not included.

papers.title: Two-Matching Popular Winning Sets for Bipartite Graphs on at Most Six Vertices
papers.problem_definition: Does every bipartite preference instance have a winning set of at most two matchings against weighted plurality comparisons?
papers.contribution: **A certificate-backed bounded-order theorem.** Proves the assertion when every connected component has at most six vertices. One pair of matchings works throughout each closed weight-order cone; 472,401,966 exact prefix inequalities certify the finite classification. The unrestricted popular-dimension question remains unresolved.

papers.title: A fixed-character gap for abelian-by-extraspecial kernels in the commuting-probability 1/97 problem
papers.problem_definition: Can an abelian-by-extraspecial kernel occur in the least-order reduction for a finite group with commuting probability $1/97$?
papers.contribution: **An infinite-family structural exclusion.** Reduces the candidate family to a fixed-character count of 107 and proves that this value lies in a forbidden gap. Covers the stated fixed-point-free cyclic action, both extraspecial exponents, and automorphisms whose cubes are inner. It does not resolve the unrestricted group-existence problem.

papers.title: No totally positive 3 by 4 matrix over F19
papers.problem_definition: Is there a $3\times4$ matrix over $\mathbb F_{19}$ whose every increasing-index minor is a nonzero square?
papers.contribution: **Negative resolution with a stronger obstruction.** Shows that even requiring only the entries and $2\times2$ minors to be nonzero squares is impossible. Positive-diagonal normalization leaves a small explicit case proof, corroborated by an exact scan of all 531,441 normalized tuples.

papers.title: An exact exclusion of three-term zero sums among algebraic conjugates of degree 28
papers.problem_definition: Can an irreducible degree-28 polynomial over $\mathbb Q$ have three distinct roots whose sum is zero?
papers.contribution: **Complete nonexistence at degree 28.** Reduces the Galois relation to triple-orbit incidence ranks for all 30 minimally transitive degree-28 actions and certifies full rational rank in every case. The group classification and general relation-module method are credited to prior work.

papers.title: The least stable threshold for four-value generalized Schur numbers
papers.problem_definition: Determine the least stable threshold in the two-color generalized Schur problem requiring exactly four distinct values among $k$ summands and their sum.
papers.contribution: **Exact formula for every admissible $k$.** Proves $S_2(k;3)=k^2+4k+3$ for all $k\ge3$, so the least stable threshold is three. Completes the cited general argument with seven independently replayed finite exclusions. This is not a theorem for arbitrary numbers of distinct values.

papers.title: Dimension one and twelve rational components of four-truncated point modules for B(Aff(3,-1),i)
papers.problem_definition: Determine the geometry of four-truncated point modules for the Nichols algebra $B(\operatorname{Aff}(3,-1),i)$ over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field.
papers.contribution: **Sharp dimension and explicit components.** Proves that the reduced parameter scheme has dimension one and contains at least twelve distinct rational irreducible components. An exhaustive chart argument and 1,428 verified polynomial identities establish the upper bound. The paper does not claim that these twelve are all components.

papers.title: Integer sums of two units in the seventh cyclotomic field
papers.problem_definition: Which positive rational integers are sums of two algebraic-integer units in $\mathbb Q(\zeta_7)$?
papers.contribution: **Complete classification: $\{1,2,3,4,5,19,22\}$.** Gives explicit unit witnesses and inverses; for sums greater than one, proves descent of both units to the maximal real subfield. The paper presents an explicit seventh-cyclotomic consequence of established cubic-field results, not a new general unit theorem.

papers.title: Affine rigidity of vector quasi-arithmetic means on closed convex domains with nonempty interior
papers.problem_definition: When does a vector quasi-arithmetic mean agree with a fixed positive-weight arithmetic mean on a full-dimensional closed convex domain, without assuming continuity of its strictly monotone generator?
papers.contribution: **Affine rigidity on all such domains.** Proves that the generator must be affine, with positive-definite symmetric linear part, and proves the converse. Local monotonicity bounds, fixed-weight Jensen regularity, and boundary interpolation extend the cited whole-space classification to bounded and unbounded closed convex domains.

papers.title: The center of distances of a duplicated base-four achievement set
papers.problem_definition: For the achievement set generated by two copies of each $4^{-p}$, determine all distances that can be realized from every point of the set to another point in it.
papers.contribution: **Exact center of distances.** Proves that the answer is precisely $\{0\}\cup\{4^{-p}:p\ge1\}$, including arbitrary real candidate distances and infinite subsums. An explicit complementary-tail obstruction excludes every other distance. The argument does not classify all semi-fast achievement sets.

papers.title: PROPX and Pareto Optimality for Three Agents and Four Chores: An Exact Certificate
papers.problem_definition: For three agents and four indivisible chores with strictly positive rational normalized costs, must a complete allocation be both proportional up to any chore and Pareto optimal among integral allocations?
papers.contribution: **Complete proof for the specified dimensions.** An exact UNSAT certificate, replayed by a solver-free rational/propositional checker, establishes existence for every admissible cost matrix. Empty bundles are allowed; Pareto comparison is against all 81 integral allocations, not fractional reallocations.

papers.title: Loewy lengths from ideal zero-product probabilities
papers.problem_definition: Do the probabilities that products of $k$ uniformly chosen ideals vanish, for all $k\ge2$, determine the multiset of local Loewy lengths of a finite commutative principal ideal ring?
papers.contribution: **Complete recovery theorem.** Equality of these probability sequences forces equality of all local Loewy lengths, including multiplicities and field factors. A least-differing-term argument in the logarithmic ratio handles unbounded lengths and numbers of factors. Nonprincipal rings are outside the theorem.

papers.title: Non-star maximizers for additive abelian Cayley completion
papers.problem_definition: Are stars the unique maximizers of the specified same-order additive abelian Cayley completion invariant?
papers.contribution: **Minimum-order counterexample and an infinite family.** For every odd $n\ge5$, constructs a non-star tree $B_n$ with $\gamma_+(B_n)=(n-2)/2$; every admissible host is complete. The least counterexample order in the stated domain is five. The proof specializes the existing parity bound rather than introducing a new general method.

papers.title: A certified upper bound of 17 for balanced rainbow-free colorings of the four-element cube
papers.problem_definition: What is the largest number of balanced color classes in $\{0,1,2,3\}^3$ such that no four-point combinatorial line is rainbow?
papers.contribution: **Improved certified upper bound: 17.** Excludes balanced 18-colorings through an exact-cover reduction on 140 columns and all 1,020 equality blocks, with a separately checked complete refutation tree. This improves the cited bound of 18; neither a 17-color construction nor the exact maximum is established.

papers.title: Minimum order of a connected cubic bipartite graph with bondage number five
papers.problem_definition: What is the minimum order of a connected simple cubic bipartite graph with bondage number five, where edge deletion increases ordinary domination number?
papers.contribution: **Exact minimum order: 18.** Certifies exclusion of all smaller graphs in the class and checks the order-18 witness. A three-perfect-matching enumeration and explicit vertex bijections support completeness. The result does not classify every minimizer at order 18.

papers.title: Binary Ferrers rank-metric codes of distance three: Singleton attainment through area 21
papers.problem_definition: Does every binary Ferrers diagram of area at most 21 admit a linear rank-metric code of minimum nonzero rank three attaining its Ferrers Singleton bound?
papers.contribution: **Complete area-21 attainment theorem.** Fourteen explicit seed codes, elementary constructions, and a verified reduction graph cover all 3,506 target partitions, including degenerate zero-code cases. The statement is finite in diagram area and does not resolve unrestricted Ferrers-code attainment.

papers.title: A Gaussian-rational degree-two counterexample to convex closure of exterior convex maps
papers.problem_definition: Can two normalized degree-two Laurent maps with Gaussian-rational coefficients both map the exterior disk onto complements of compact convex sets, while their midpoint fails this property?
papers.contribution: **Explicit positive answer to the counterexample-existence question.** Gives two exact maps with finite Laurent tails, proves univalence and convexity by rational certificates, and exhibits a strict midpoint curvature violation. This disproves convex closure in the specified degree-two class; it does not assert failure of the original existential question.

papers.title: Three zero-length wormholes on a circle: the sharp diameter is one quarter
papers.problem_definition: How small can the intrinsic diameter of a circle become after adding at most three zero-length pair identifications, allowing repeated or shared endpoints?
papers.contribution: **Sharp value: one quarter of the circumference.** Proves the universal lower bound and supplies an attaining two-identification construction. A finite multigraph classification and rational inequality certificates include degenerate arc lengths. No general theorem for larger odd wormhole budgets is claimed.

papers.title: The minimum signed spectral radius of C20(1,2)
papers.problem_definition: Among all edge signings of the circulant graph $C_{20}(1,2)$, minimize the maximum absolute adjacency eigenvalue and classify equality.
papers.contribution: **Exact minimum and both equality classes.** The optimum is $2\sqrt{\cos^2(\pi/20)+\cos^2(\pi/10)}$. Integer Rayleigh witnesses, an overlap-graph argument, and exact exceptional-polynomial checks prove the lower bound; every other switching class has a strict certified gap. The all-even-order conjecture is not settled.

papers.title: A three-generator monomial ideal whose v-number increases under integral closure
papers.problem_definition: Must integral closure weakly decrease the $v$-number of every proper monomial ideal with at most three minimal generators?
papers.contribution: **Three-generator counterexample over every field.** For $J=(y^2,yz^3,x^3z^4)$, proves $v(J)=3$ but $v(\overline J)=4$. Gives the exact integral closure, prime-colon witnesses, and lower bounds valid for arbitrary homogeneous polynomial witnesses, including embedded-prime possibilities.

papers.title: Recognizing SL2(7) by its order and conjugacy class sizes
papers.problem_definition: Is a finite group of order 336 uniquely determined up to isomorphism by the conjugacy-class-size set $\{1,24,42,56\}$?
papers.contribution: **Recognition of $\mathrm{SL}_2(7)$.** Proves uniqueness using structural deductions and a complete 228-group catalogue computation. The sole survivor is matched to explicit matrices modulo seven by a bijection checked on every product. The result requires the group order; it is not an order-free characterization.

papers.title: Random-cluster edge correlations on graphs with at most six vertices
papers.problem_definition: For the homogeneous random-cluster model with $0<p,q<1$, are distinct edge indicators negatively correlated on every connected simple graph with at most six vertices?
papers.contribution: **Complete bounded-order theorem for all real parameters.** Every covariance numerator factors as $(q-1)$ times a polynomial with nonnegative coefficients. Independent exact implementations verify all 4,208 edge pairs in 143 representatives and certify graph coverage. Larger graphs, inhomogeneous activities, and full negative association remain outside the claim.

papers.title: A strict gap between square isolation and domination in the six-dimensional cube
papers.problem_definition: Is the square-isolation number of the $n$-cube always the domination number of the $(n-2)$-cube?
papers.contribution: **Exact counterexample in dimension six.** Proves $\iota(Q_6,Q_2)=5$ while $\gamma(Q_4)=4$. An explicit five-vertex isolating set attains the bound, and exhaustive exact certificates exclude every four-set. This disproves the universal identity without claiming the first failing dimension.

papers.title: Affine versus permutation equivalence of cubic monomial rotation symmetric Boolean functions in 33 variables
papers.problem_definition: For cubic monomial rotation-symmetric Boolean functions in 33 variables, does equivalence under an arbitrary invertible affine input substitution imply equivalence under a coordinate permutation?
papers.contribution: **Complete dimension-33 classification.** Twelve multiplier orbits are separated by weights, exact Walsh-moment invariants, and cubic-polar contraction ranks. Includes translations in the affine substitutions. The analogous assertion in every dimension remains outside the result.

papers.title: An endpoint-majority condition for three-point Grunbaum rate-distortion maximizers
papers.problem_definition: Determine the extremizers and exact value in the specified three-point Grünbaum rate-distortion optimization problem.
papers.contribution: **A structural restriction on every maximizer.** Proves that a maximizing three-point law must place mass strictly greater than one half at an endpoint. A rigorous Gaussian-mixture bound excludes both endpoint-nonmajority chambers. The exact extremal value and full optimizer classification remain unresolved.

papers.title: A 96-element Sidon subset of the seventeenth multinomial coefficient layer
papers.problem_definition: What is the largest Sidon subset of the distinct multinomial coefficients arising from partitions of 17, with repeated-element pair sums included?
papers.contribution: **Explicit improvement of the lower bound to 96.** Supplies one partition witness for each selected value and verifies all 4,656 unordered pair sums are distinct. This improves the cited bound of 89 by seven. It does not exclude a 97-element set or prove optimality.

papers.title: Positive integer solutions of a symmetric generalized Markov equation
papers.problem_definition: For which positive integers $k$ does $x^2+y^2+z^2+xy+xz+yz=kxyz$ have positive integer solutions, and how are all such solutions generated?
papers.contribution: **Complete parameter and orbit classification.** Solutions exist exactly for $k\in\{1,2,3,6\}$; each solution lies in the permutation-and-Vieta orbit of $(6/k,6/k,6/k)$. Descent and an exact terminal classification cover every positive solution. The known $k=6$ case is credited to prior work.

papers.title: Five star tests suffice for the hexagon: the minimum and all attaining interval families
papers.problem_definition: For a cyclically labelled hexagon, find the smallest fixed family of consecutive-interval star tests detecting every nonlocal chord multiset of total multiplicity at most three.
papers.contribution: **Sharp minimum and every attaining family.** Proves that five tests are necessary and sufficient. Classifies nine quotient minimizers, corresponding to thirty families of the original intervals, and includes repeated-chord and empty-support cases. No general-polygon optimum is asserted.

papers.title: The 3,371 semiaffine orbits of order-four anti-coordinate grid decompositions
papers.problem_definition: Classify compatible unordered pairs of anti-coordinate four-block partitions of $\mathbb F_4^2$ under simultaneous semiaffine transformations.
papers.contribution: **Complete census: 3,371 orbits.** Gives a canonical representative and full stabilizer for every orbit, covering 18,954,720 compatible pairs. Independent constructions verify both domain completeness and the group action. The classification is specifically for order four.

papers.title: A minimal counterexample to Class 69 mesh-pattern equidistribution on involutions
papers.problem_definition: Are the two specified Class 69 mesh patterns equidistributed by occurrence count on involutions, including fixed points?
papers.contribution: **Minimal hand-checkable counterexample.** At order three the occurrence polynomials are $2+y+y^2$ and $1+2y+y^2$; all smaller orders agree. The paper reconstructs the source coordinates and refutes the displayed conjecture in the cited version, without claiming a statement about later revisions.

papers.title: An optimal acyclic-pivot certificate for the degree-seven Peterson hit matrix in three variables
papers.problem_definition: For the degree-seven Peterson hit matrix in three variables over $\mathbb F_2$, what is the largest acyclic-pivot family using only original labelled columns?
papers.contribution: **Exact acyclic-pivot optimum: 26.** Constructs 26 eligible columns with an acyclic pivot assignment and proves a matching rank upper bound from ten left annihilators. The matrix rank itself was already known; the contribution is the optimal original-column certificate and its structural proof.

papers.title: A full-rank qubit counterexample to data processing for a trace-exponential relative functional
papers.problem_definition: Does $S_2^Q(A\Vert B)=\log\operatorname{Tr}[A\exp(\log A-\log B)]$ satisfy data processing under every quantum channel on positive-definite qubit states?
papers.contribution: **Strict full-rank qubit counterexample.** Gives exact Bloch vectors and an amplitude-damping channel whose trace-exponential value increases from a certified interval near 7.5410 to one near 8.3778. Rational interval bounds establish the strict violation without relying on singular-state ambiguities or floating-point comparisons.

papers.title: An exact census of symmetric chain decompositions of M(6)
papers.problem_definition: How many symmetric chain decompositions does the strict-partition poset $M(6)$ have, counting decompositions on the fixed poset rather than modulo symmetry?
papers.contribution: **Certified census of 1,344 decompositions.** Exact cover over all 75,584 eligible symmetric paths and an independently checked counting recurrence prove completeness. The contribution is the durable upper-bound certificate and census; the numerical value and the existence of these decompositions were already recorded.

papers.title: A six-term progression in a cap-six additive basis modulo 29
papers.problem_definition: In $\mathbb Z/29\mathbb Z$, how long can a distinct-term arithmetic progression be inside an additive basis whose ordered two-sum representation counts all lie between one and six?
papers.contribution: **Counterexample and corrected exact maximum: six.** The set $\{0,1,2,3,4,5,8,13,19,23\}$ violates the proposed maximum of five. Exact representation counts certify admissibility, and the endpoint-pair bound proves optimality for the fixed cap. This is not a result for infinitely many moduli.

papers.title: An infinite binary word avoiding Cartesian-tree squares of half-length at least four
papers.problem_definition: Does an infinite binary word exist with no adjacent blocks of equal Cartesian-tree shape whenever their common length is at least four, using the leftmost-minimum tie rule?
papers.contribution: **Explicit infinite construction.** A four-uniform coding of a specially constrained square-free ternary source avoids every forbidden block length. A synchronization argument handles all long factors, with complete exact checks for the finite remainder. The coding is not claimed to work for arbitrary ternary square-free sources.

papers.title: Reconstructing permutations of order eleven from five-element patterns
papers.problem_definition: What is the least pattern-deck size that reconstructs every permutation of order eleven?
papers.contribution: **Exact reconstruction threshold: five.** Sixteen marginals of the five-pattern deck distinguish all 39,916,800 permutations; an explicit known four-deck collision supplies the lower bound. Two exact implementations establish injectivity without treating probabilistic fingerprints as equality certificates. No threshold beyond order eleven is asserted.

papers.title: The prescribed-parity induced-subgraph minimum on eleven vertices
papers.problem_definition: For every eleven-vertex graph without isolated vertices and every prescribed vertex-parity labeling, how large an induced subgraph satisfying all its prescribed degree parities is guaranteed?
papers.contribution: **Exact guaranteed size: four.** Checked refutations cover every labeling weight for the lower bound. A complementary-cycle construction with two disjoint edges supplies a matching example whose largest admissible subset has size four. The result includes disconnected graphs but is restricted to order eleven.

papers.title: Central-inversion-invariant domination on the 7 x 7 x 7 queen graph
papers.problem_definition: Determine the minimum dominating-set size in the nonperiodic $7\times7\times7$ queen graph.
papers.contribution: **Exact answer within the central-inversion-invariant class: twelve.** Combines a twelve-queen witness with a checked exclusion of every smaller invariant set. Any unrestricted improvement must therefore break central inversion. The unrestricted domination number is not determined or improved.

papers.title: The permanent spectrum of cubic zero-one matrices of order twelve
papers.problem_definition: Which permanent values occur among all $12\times12$ zero-one matrices whose row and column sums are three, including disconnected incidence graphs?
papers.contribution: **Complete spectrum of 189 values.** Provides one matrix per value, combines connected spectra with every component-product type, and proves completeness by exact orbit mass against an independent labelled-matrix count. Nineteen values were absent from the saved 170-value example list.

papers.title: Full trace-profile fibres of traceless matrix triples over F5
papers.problem_definition: Among traceless $2\times2$ matrix triples over $\mathbb F_5$, how many simultaneous-conjugacy orbits can share the traces of every nonempty matrix word?
papers.contribution: **Exact maximum and unique maximizing profile.** The maximum is 32, attained only by the identically zero trace profile; its orbits have an explicit projective classification. Every nonzero profile has one or thirteen orbits. Structural arguments and complete exact enumerations cover degenerate and nonsemisimple triples.

papers.title: The induced-forest number of the Higman--Sims graph
papers.problem_definition: What is the largest induced forest in the 100-vertex Higman–Sims graph, allowing disconnected forests?
papers.contribution: **Exact induced-forest number: 26.** Gives an induced-tree witness and a spectral-rank proof excluding every 27-vertex forest; the minimum feedback vertex set is therefore 74. The upper bound does not rely on a timed-out SAT search. Maximizers are not fully classified.

papers.title: Bounds for triple separation in the Witt design
papers.problem_definition: How many octads of the Witt design $S(5,8,24)$ are needed to give distinct containment signatures to all 2,024 triples, with the zero signature allowed?
papers.contribution: **Improved rigorous interval: $90\le m(W)\le127$.** Weight-two signature charges and second moments prove the lower bound; an explicit 127-octad family certifies the upper bound. This narrows the project-verified interval $[81,130]$ but does not identify the exact minimum.

papers.title: An exact polynomial and rational certification of the symmetric five-node Lebesgue optimum
papers.problem_definition: Minimize the Lebesgue constant for interpolation at the symmetric five-node set $\{-1,-a,0,a,1\}$ over all $0<a<1$.
papers.contribution: **Exact algebraic certification of the unique optimum.** Proves uniqueness, derives an irreducible degree-73 polynomial for $a_*\approx0.620911304689912040$, and encloses the sharp constant near 1.559490209875555264 by exact rationals. Classical general equioscillation theory is background; the explicit polynomial and certification are the added result.

papers.title: Four-cycle supersaturation at orders 19, 20, and 21
papers.problem_definition: How few four-cycles can a graph contain when it has one more edge than the $C_4$-free extremal threshold?
papers.contribution: **Exact small-order values.** Establishes $h(19)=2$ and $h(20)=h(21)=3$, with the substantive new finite exclusion at orders 20 and 21. Uses explicitly attributed small-order extremal data and a complete near-extremal census. The original asymptotic supersaturation question remains unresolved.

papers.title: No connected nontraceable detour graph has ten vertices
papers.problem_definition: Is there a connected nontraceable graph on ten vertices in which every vertex is an endpoint of a longest path?
papers.contribution: **Complete order-ten exclusion.** A cut-vertex reduction and exact per-graph certificates cover all 9,743,542 biconnected classes, either producing a Hamilton path or an unequal endpoint-length vector. This also excludes the specifically requested longest-path order nine; no global minimum-order theorem is claimed.

papers.title: Rule 37 under fixed sequential updates: a minimum six-cell cover and a resistant twelve-cell state
papers.problem_definition: For cellular automaton Rule 37 with a fixed sequential update permutation repeated forever, can a state resist all update orders, and how many orders suffice to cover the six-cell states?
papers.contribution: **A resistant twelve-cell witness and a sharp six-cell correction.** Proves resistance of the explicit twelve-cell state under every fixed permutation. At six cells, exactly three update orders suffice for full basin coverage, contradicting a specific six-cell resistance assertion in the inspected source. No arbitrary-ring-size classification is claimed.

papers.title: Three-uniform word representations of all bipartite graphs with parts of size six
papers.problem_definition: Does every bipartite graph with two parts of size six admit a word representation in which each vertex occurs exactly three times?
papers.contribution: **Complete $6+6$ theorem.** Certifies all 251,610 fixed-part isomorphism classes; structural reductions and cited theorems cover most cases, while explicit independently checked words cover the 8,677 residual classes. Isolated vertices, disconnected graphs, and repeated neighborhoods are included.

papers.title: An explicit 64-modular Hadamard matrix of order 892
papers.problem_definition: Does there exist an order-892 sign matrix satisfying $HH^\mathsf T\equiv892I\pmod{64}$?
papers.contribution: **Explicit modular Hadamard construction.** Supplies a full sign matrix and proves the stronger identity $HH^\mathsf T=380I_{892}+512(I_4\otimes J_{223})$ using a periodic complementary quadruple. Both direct integer checks and a support-intersection proof certify it. This is not an ordinary Hadamard matrix.

papers.title: A cubic graph on sixteen vertices without an equitable four-total coloring
papers.problem_definition: Must a cubic graph of order below twenty that admits a proper four-total coloring also admit an equitable one?
papers.contribution: **Connected sixteen-vertex counterexample.** Gives a proper four-total coloring but proves that no equitable four-total coloring exists, through a gadget argument and a checked refutation certificate. The paper does not claim that sixteen is the minimum counterexample order.

papers.title: A 2-primary Smith condition for maximal binary rank of skew walk matrices
papers.problem_definition: For a controllable oriented graph, does square-freeness of the largest Smith invariant of its skew walk matrix force maximal binary rank?
papers.contribution: **A stronger 2-primary theorem.** For every integer skew-symmetric matrix with nonsingular walk matrix, the weaker condition $4\nmid d_n$ already implies binary rank $\lceil n/2\rceil$. A localized cyclic-lattice argument and an alternating-form obstruction prove the statement without restricting to graph matrices.

papers.title: Permutation crossword grids with one or two complete rook placements
papers.problem_definition: When does a permutation crossword grid admit exactly one or two complete rook placements, meeting each maximal white across and down word once?
papers.contribution: **Complete characterization by skew-merged permutations.** Proves that every non-skew-merged permutation has at least three complete placements, completing the cited equivalence. Extremal deletion, terminal-family classification, and explicit three-placement constructions supply the new direction; the forward implication is credited to prior work.

papers.title: Nonexistence of invertible cross-product twists for gl2(F)/(FI) in characteristic two
papers.problem_definition: Over a characteristic-two field, can $\mathfrak{gl}_2(F)/(FI)$ be identified with $F^3$ so that its Lie bracket is an invertible linear twist of the coordinate cross product?
papers.contribution: **Nonexistence over every such field.** A trace obstruction and an independent rank comparison rule out every invertible twist, without finiteness or perfection assumptions. An explicit singular rank-two twist shows exactly why invertibility matters. The result concerns $\mathfrak{gl}_2/(FI)$, not a quotient of $\mathfrak{sl}_2$.

papers.title: The relative dimension of the four-dimensional Boolean lattice
papers.problem_definition: What is the minimum total length of a local realizer of the sixteen-element Boolean lattice $B_4$, and hence its relative dimension?
papers.contribution: **Exact total length 42 and relative dimension $21/8$.** Gives four attaining partial linear extensions and excludes all shorter realizers using rational dual bounds and a checked final refutation. Also determines the fractional covering optimum as $202/5$. The asymptotic Boolean-lattice problem is not resolved.

papers.title: Necessity of admissible angles for the periods c+a and c+b in three-move subtraction games
papers.problem_definition: In a three-move subtraction game, do pure Sprague–Grundy periods $c+a$ and $c+b$ force the corresponding admissible-angle conditions?
papers.contribution: **Both necessity implications, in a stronger form.** Proves the conditions already for zero/nonzero outcome periods from zero, without requiring coprimality or leastness. Explicit seam mismatches and a circular difference-set identity settle the cited two implications. The full classification of purely periodic three-move games is not claimed.

papers.title: A Sign Classification of Total-Word Additive Level Sorts
papers.problem_definition: For a word transformation that sorts letters by their cumulative integer starting levels, with either positional scan direction breaking ties, when is the transformation polyregular?
papers.contribution: **Complete sign classification.** The transformation is polyregular exactly when all weights have the same weak sign; these cases admit explicit arity-one first-order transductions. A uniform distinguishability argument excludes every mixed-sign case. The domain is all words, not only a restricted balanced-word language.

papers.title: A uniform upper bound for Hamiltonian graphs of minimum degree three
papers.problem_definition: Determine the eventual-order threshold for Hamiltonian graphs of minimum degree three with no cycle of length two less than their order.
papers.contribution: **Uniform construction for every $n\ge19$.** Gives graphs with exactly $2n-5$ edges and minimum degree exactly three, proving the threshold is at most 19. A fan-interface argument extends the known seed through all orders. Nonexistence at order 18, needed for an exact threshold, is not certified.

papers.title: Disjoint-union bounds for the continuous theta saturation parameter
papers.problem_definition: Study the continuous theta-saturation parameter under graph operations and the proposed global inequality relating it to the Lovász theta function.
papers.contribution: **Disjoint-union bounds and a counterexample reduction.** Proves upper and lower union bounds, exact formulas under the theta-product equality hypothesis, and additivity under joins. A smallest counterexample to the original inequality must be connected with connected complement. Exact checks cover order at most six; the global inequality remains unresolved.

papers.title: Degree recovery from the ordinary loopy polynomial on a recognizable class of looped multigraphs
papers.problem_definition: Does the ordinary loopy polynomial determine the degree multiset of a looped multigraph, counting each loop twice?
papers.contribution: **Explicit recovery on an unbounded recognizable class.** Derives a nonlinear recovery formula when each vertex has at most one loop and parallel edges between two unlooped vertices are absent. Parallel edges incident to looped vertices remain unrestricted. The class itself is recognizable from the polynomial; the unrestricted problem is not settled.

papers.title: The fixed-order minimum L5(5)=72
papers.problem_definition: What is the minimum diameter of a five-element integer alphabet whose order-five multiset sums are all distinct?
papers.contribution: **Exact value $L_5(5)=72$.** The alphabet $(0,1,16,66,72)$ attains the bound. Explicit balanced-relation rejection certificates exclude every smaller-diameter alphabet, independently covering the entire finite domain. No general-order formula or classification of all minimizers is asserted.

papers.title: An eleven-vertex tournament with no simultaneously optimal backedge ordering
papers.problem_definition: Does every tournament have a vertex ordering simultaneously minimizing the clique number and chromatic number of its backedge graph?
papers.contribution: **Explicit eleven-vertex counterexample.** The separate minima are two and three, but the unique triangle-free backedge ordering has chromatic number four. Exact full-permutation and valid-prefix enumerations establish uniqueness, supported by a direct coloring obstruction. Minimum counterexample order is not claimed.

papers.title: Eulerian orientations of separable 4-regular graphs on sixteen vertices
papers.problem_definition: What is the maximum number of Eulerian orientations of a connected separable simple 4-regular graph on sixteen vertices, and does the proposed universal bound hold?
papers.contribution: **Exact maximum 9,216, with one extremal isomorphism class.** The unique maximizer violates the proposed bound by an exact ratio $256/243$ after taking seventh powers. Complete branch generation and independent orientation counts certify the upper bound and equality classification. Other graph orders are not classified.

papers.title: Minimum resolving families in the six-element Jaccard space
